clue.text: Jelly and Sara's pistachio ice cream to sample when opening …

indicators.note: we sample only the opening of each word in the list, its first letter

explanation.surface: A dessert menu pairing jelly with Sara's pistachio ice cream, offered as tasters on opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 4 across: it is the opening night of Sara's wine bar, and the trailing dots carry the story on.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine in which meats or eggs are set, a kind of jelly.

clue.text: See 4
Ringing hot teenagers up for modelling this Sun exclusive?

definitions.text: Ringing hot teenagers up for modelling this Sun exclusive?

indicators.note: modelling reshapes the pool of letters into a new form
the word group teenagers up is said to ring, that is surround, the next piece

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the letters of the newspaper's name are the ones left over, excluded from the result

explanation.surface: A tabloid trumpets its exclusive about young people posing for photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exclusive' tells you the letters of SUN are left out of the rearranged pool; the whole clue also describes the old topless-model feature of the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun, a British tabloid, long ran photos of topless models on its third leaf, a feature known by that leaf number.

clue.text: In pop art our works embellished in bars

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the drink word

parts.note: pop is a fizzy drink, such as cola

indicators.note: works as a verb: the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A comment on pop art in which our own works are decorated with bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop art' reads as a phrase, but 'pop' is the drink and 'art our' is the fodder that 'works' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloratura describes vocal music richly ornamented with runs and trills, embellished passages within the bars of a score.

clue.text: … Sara's Yuppie Wine Bar — not a bad job I've done (it was 27 asking him …)

definitions.text: Sara's Yuppie Wine Bar — not a bad job I've done (it was 27 asking him

parts.words: Sara's Yuppie Wine Bar — not a bad job I've done (it was 27 asking him
parts.note: Sara's Yuppie Wine Bar, less an A, shuffles ('bad') into the second half of the saying; the setter has organised that rearrangement, the man asked could not, as he was no use

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of having put on a launch party for Sara's trendy wine bar, since nobody else could be trusted to.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds only the second half of the phrase: SARA'S YUPPIE WINE BAR, 'not a' (one A dropped) and rearranged ('bad'), gives the party in the brewery; the rest is the story of who failed to arrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying describes a hopelessly incompetent person, someone who could not manage even the easiest event.

clue.text: I really can't stand attending this woman's tours

indicators.note: tours is read as goes round, so the woman's word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: her is the possessive for this woman
attending an event means being at it

explanation.surface: Someone complains they cannot bear to go on this woman's tours.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who says they really cannot stand a thing is one who detests it, a person full of loathing.

clue.text: Touch and go, declare a firm almost completely bust? It's 27

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters fall into a new order
almost the whole word is used, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A firm on the brink declares itself all but bankrupt in a touch-and-go situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' drops the M of FIRM; the anagram gives a classic image of uselessness, 27 across being NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireguard made of chocolate would melt at once, a stock example of something that serves no purpose.

clue.text: See 4
Saw out of the ark

definitions.meaning: saw as the past tense of see, as in going out with someone romantically
out of Noah's ark, meaning very old-fashioned

explanation.definitionFit: To be going out with someone is to court them, and anything antique or old-fashioned is behind the times.

clue.text: See 11
Take one OK game to subdue court favourite

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: subdue is read as hold down or contain, so these pieces close round the next

parts.note: go is a board game
taken as written
to let something happen is to OK it

explanation.surface: Instructions for a card or board game in which the court favourite must be brought under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to subdue' means the game and 'to' hold the OK word down between them; 'Take' is the prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's hunchbacked jester, the favourite entertainer at the Duke of Mantua's court.

clue.text: Not all the mail to be answered privately?

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, its final letter being dropped

parts.note: an in-tray holds letters still to be dealt with

explanation.surface: An office question about which post should be answered in private.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Latin prefix for within, as in matters kept inside a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin prefix means within, matters kept inside a body, a loose fit for done in private.

clue.text: For revitalising, get a pot for a brew, then put one in? It's 27

indicators.note: put one in: the single letter goes inside the shuffled letters
revitalising means renewing, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A as the indefinite article means one

explanation.surface: Instructions for perking up a cup of tea: get a pot to brew, then add one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For revitalising' shuffles GET A POT FOR A BREW, and 'put ... in' adds one more A; the result is a stock emblem of uselessness, 27 across being NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag that let no water through could never brew, the very picture of a thing with no purpose.

clue.text: Authenticate each plan

parts.note: to ID someone is to identify or verify them

explanation.surface: A business instruction to verify every proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or scheme in the mind is a notion, synonym of the clue's noun.

clue.text: Occupying ground floor pad, oozed craft food? It's 27

parts.note: occupying a place means being in it
a pad is a flat, and the ground-floor one in a building is often labelled flat A
blood oozing from a wound means it bled
craft means skill or artistry
board means meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone living in a ground-floor flat leaks home-made food everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The result is a stock emblem of uselessness, 27 across being NO USE: darts would simply bounce off.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-up target for darts would burst at the first throw, a byword for something with no purpose.

clue.text: Moralist priest lost in valley submerged Land of Hope

indicators.note: the shortened moralist sits inside the valley word

parts.note: a ria is a drowned river valley

indicators.note: the priest is lost, taken away from the word

parts.note: a puritan is a strict moralist

explanation.surface: A preacher of morals disappears in a flooded valley in the land of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Hope' is not the patriotic song: Anthony Hope wrote The Prisoner of Zenda, set in this imaginary kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's novels.

clue.text: Not killing time — extra working hours

indicators.note: extra means something added, here slipped into the first word

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working
the Ides of March was the time of Caesar's assassination

explanation.surface: Advice not to idle away overtime spent working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing time' looks like idling; it is the Ides, when Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontides are the midday periods, a poetic word for times of day around twelve.

clue.text: Rebuffed lover's fine bulging pants

indicators.note: the reversed word bulges with an extra letter inside it
rebuffed suggests pushed back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a fan is a lover of something
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A spurned lover's tight trousers are bursting at the seams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, as is the answer: not underwear here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, pants as an adjective means poor or rubbish, the same as naff, meaning tacky.

clue.text: See 5
Newspaper boss comes in to try uplifting Greek dish

indicators.note: the newspaper boss comes into the other word
uplifting in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to seek is to try
FT is the Financial Times
ED is short for editor, the boss of a paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor drops in to sample an uplifting Greek dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifting' reverses only the verb for try; the newspaper boss then comes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keftedes are Greek meatballs, a common meze dish.

clue.text: Awry, staggering out of 1D, this drunk?

indicators.note: staggering means reeling, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: 1 down reads A BREWERY

explanation.surface: Someone staggering out of a brewery, this drunk, has gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes the letters of AWRY away from A BREWERY; 'staggering' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is the thing a brewery makes and drinkers have drunk, the 'this' of the definition.

clue.text: Too big: integral, revolutionary

annotationWithheld.why: Too big: integral, revolutionary (9): the answer is hidden reversed in 'integral, revolutionary', but no word signals the hiding: 'revolutionary' is both the reversal indicator and part of the hidden text, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Accompanying second piano, a fan of dramatic voice

parts.note: P is the musical direction piano, softly
to be into something is to be a fan of it

explanation.surface: A singer's admirer is accompanying a second piano part.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinto is a lyric operatic voice with dramatic power, between lyric and heavier types.

clue.text: See 4
Wounded privates picked up German

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is picked up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: nuts is slang for testicles, privates

explanation.surface: Injured soldiers are collected by a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' looks like soldiers; it is slang for the private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stung means hurt or wounded, especially in feelings.

clue.text: Disgruntled at times about the origin of Tunbridge Wells? 11 in another state

indicators.note: disgruntled means put out, so these letters are put out of order
about means turned round, so the town's first letter and the author's initials read backwards together
the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: H. G. Wells, the author, gives his initials

explanation.surface: A grumpy letter-writer from Tunbridge Wells, complaining about the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns T plus HG into GHT. The surface nods to 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells', the stereotypical angry letter-writer from that genteel English town; 11 across is WATERPROOF, and steam is water in another state.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamtight means sealed against steam, as waterproof is against water: steam is water as vapour.

clue.text: Gold being carried up to a vital transporter

indicators.note: the gold is carried inside the other pieces
in a down clue up reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: at can mean to, as in going at or to a target
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold is being carried up to a vital transport link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for to, in a down clue read bottom to top; 'being carried' puts the heraldic gold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, carrying blood from the heart, a vital transporter.

clue.text: Paltry average

definitions.meaning: paltry ... stingy or small, as in a miserly sum
the arithmetic average of a set of numbers

explanation.definitionFit: Mean can mean stingy or meagre, and in statistics it is the average value.

clue.text: Reviewing the options you finally get given on Pointless?

indicators.note: reviewing is read as viewing again backwards, so the letters run in reverse
finally takes the last letter of each word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A contestant on the TV quiz Pointless reviews the options before answering.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is a BBC quiz show where contestants seek obscure answers; here the word is just an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless serves no purpose, a phrase meaning of no help.

clue.text: See 13
See 4
It's how society expresses itself, so stop being "retro"

indicators.note: retro means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A remark that a society expresses itself through style, so stop being nostalgic.
explanation.walkthrough: SO DIE read backwards; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidos is the distinctive outlook or character expressed by a culture, its intellectual ethos.
